{{nihongo|'''Iwafune Shrine'''|石船神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Iwafune Shrine''' (いわふねじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Murakami, Niigata|Q284503|qid=Q284503}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|Q132705|qid=Q132705}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shikinai shrine}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, and is the foremost of the eight shrines of {{ill|Iwafune District, Niigata|Q1155124|qid=Q1155124|lt=Iwafune District}}<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1273537/1/102 |title=Engishiki Vol. 2 |access-date=2024-5-6}}</ref><ref name="tourism">[https://www.sake3.com/spot/858 Iwafune Shrine] Murakami City Tourism Association “Murakami City Tourism Information Dispatch Base”</ref><ref name="walk">Editorial Committee of *Historical Walks of Niigata Prefecture*, ed., *Historical Walks of Niigata Prefecture (Historical Walks 15)*, Yamakawa Shuppansha, 2009, pp. 214–215</ref>.

Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}} of the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, it was ranked as the first {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}} in Niigata Prefecture<ref name="tourism" />.

=== History ===
The shrine is enshrined on the southern foothills of Myojin-yama.

It is said that the shrine already existed at the time the {{ill|Iwafuke Palisade|Q11587922|qid=Q11587922}} was established, prior to {{ill|648|Q30618|qid=Q30618}} (Taika 4), meaning it must have been founded even earlier. Although the location of the Iwanofune stockade remains unknown, there is a theory that it was located near this shrine. Archaeological investigations conducted in 1957–1958 uncovered stone-paved structural remains and dwelling sites, and this area has been tentatively identified as the site of the Iwanofune stockade<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://engishiki.org/echigo/bun/ecg360701-01.html |title=Iwafune Shrine |access-date=2024-5-6}}</ref>. The *Echigo Nayori* records that {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}} “arrived riding the stone ship, the {{ill|Ama-no-iwafune|Q126914107|qid=Q126914107}}”<ref>From *Studies on Shikinai Shrines*, Vol. 8</ref>.

In {{ill|807|Q30016|qid=Q30016}} ({{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} 2), {{ill|Akishino no Yasuhito|Q11595792|qid=Q11595792}}, an inspector of the {{ill|Hokurikudō|Q3139239|qid=Q3139239}} region, constructed the shrine buildings<ref name="tourism"></ref>. At that time, a divided spirit of {{ill|Kifune Shrine|abstract|Q276779|fr|Kifune-jinja|ja|貴船神社|ko|기후네 신사|my|ခိဖုနဲနတ်ကျောင်း|ru|Кифунэ-дзиндзя|zh|貴船神社|qid=Q276779}} (Sakyō-ku, Kyoto City) was {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|ja|合祀|qid=Q11412524}} and {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|ja|合祀|qid=Q11412524}}.

In {{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shōtoku}} 4 (1714), the shrine was granted the divine rank of {{ill|Senior First Rank|Q11123258|qid=Q11123258}}.

Within the shrine, a sacred boat called “Myojin-maru (Ofune-sama)” is enshrined, said to be the vessel used when the deity descended from the divine realm to the human world. In contrast to {{ill|Yata ni Imasu Kushitamahiko Shrine|Q11584205|qid=Q11584205}} in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}, which is regarded as a deity of air transportation, this shrine is believed to have a strong association with maritime transportation.

=== Enshrined deities ===
Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto; {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mizuhanome-no-Mikoto}}; {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takaokami-no-Kami}}; {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kuraokami-no-Kami}}.

=== Auxiliary shrines ===
* Wakayama Shrine and Konpira Shrine  
* Myojin Gongen Shrine  
* Ōyamatsumi Shrine  
* Furu Mine Shrine  
* Iwafune Shōkon Shrine, among others

=== Cultural properties ===
* Iwafune Shrine Sacred Forest (designated Natural Monument of Niigata Prefecture, designated March 5, 1958)<ref name="pref">[https://www.pref.niigata.lg.jp/uploaded/life/602399_1719772_misc.pdf List of Designated Cultural Properties] Niigata Prefecture / Japan</ref>
* Shagiri float procession and the “Tomoyama” ritual of the Iwafune Festival<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.city.murakami.lg.jp/site/kanko/iwafune-taisai.html |title=Iwafune Grand Festival |access-date=2024-5-7}}</ref> (designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Niigata Prefecture on March 25, 1988)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pref.niigata.lg.jp/uploaded/life/602399_1719772_misc.pdf |title=National and Niigata Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties |access-date=2024-5-7}}</ref>

=== Access ===
* 40-minute walk from {{ill|Iwafunemachi Station|Q6100285|qid=Q6100285}} on the {{ill|Japan Railways Group|Q864495|qid=Q864495}} {{ill|Uetsu Main Line|Q1056211|qid=Q1056211}}
* 20 minutes by bus bound for Iwafune or Shioya from {{ill|Murakami Station (Niigata)|Q6937257|qid=Q6937257|lt=Murakami Station}} on the JR Uetsu Main Line; get off at “Iwafune Shrine-mae” bus stop, immediately nearby
